messages:
PagerBot: PagerDuty alert — GPU pool eu-west-1: available_nodes=0, autoscaler_state=AtMax, queue_length=834, throttled=432 (2026-03-15T09:12:00Z)
Maya (oncall): i'm seeing the same on dashboard. latency spike around 09:10, 503s on generation API. taking it. assigning to @sam
Sam (sre): on it. initial triage: autoscaler rejected new nodes due to max_nodes=80 on nodepool-gpu-eu-west. HC events show pod pending because of quota on pods-per-node? investigating.
Ava (support): getting customer DMs — ~6 customers reporting timeouts on embeddings and batch jobs. Told them we're triaging, ETA unknown.
Devon (infra): confirming pool config: 
```
gcloud container node-pools describe nodepool-gpu-eu-west --cluster=redwood-prod-eu
maxNodes: 80
autoscaling: enabled
minNodes: 10
```
Looks like policy cap at cloud side + internal safety gate.
Sam (sre): metrics: queue growth rate +120r/s, average token latency up 4x. KV cache hit unchanged. Seems demand spike + some long-running jobs pinning GPUs.
Maya (oncall): priority = high. customer impact = partial degradation for hosted inference; dedicated customers unaffected. Ava, keep support patch loop active and collect customer ids with errors.
Ava (support): ack — collecting logs + request ids. will post a list in ~10m.
Sam (sre): quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending | head` shows ~62 pending gpu pods with reason: "ExceededNodeGroupCapacity" and some "ImagePullBackOff" mixed in.
Devon (infra): ImagePullBackOff small % (old build), not the root cause. ExceededNodeGroupCapacity = autoscaler hit max_nodes. need human cap raise or quick scale to alternative pool.
Maya (oncall): what's our runway if we do nothing?
Sam (sre): at current arrival rate ~15m before queue doubles and errors spike to >20% sustained.
Maya (oncall): manual cap raise procedure needed. Devon do we need approval? ops policy requires 2-person signoff for temporary node increases >+20 nodes during business hours.
Devon (infra): correct. we can do an emergency bump via infra-admin console for 2h window. steps: 1) set cloud maxNodes to 120, 2) disable safety gate for this cluster, 3) watch autoscaler. I'll prepare the command and require @maya confirmation.
Maya (oncall): i authorize emergency bump +20 nodes now. Sam, will you shadow the change and watch logs?
Sam (sre): i'm watching. also will cordon suspicious long-running jobs if they are low priority.
OpsBot: Incident policy: log entry created (INC-2026-0315-172), runbook: gpu-autoscale-exceeded.
Devon (infra): running command now: 
```
# infra-admin console / gcloud equivalent
gcloud container node-pools update nodepool-gpu-eu-west \
  --cluster=redwood-prod-eu --enable-autoprovisioning --max-nodes=120
```
Devon (infra): change submitted, cloud accepted. autoscaler reconciliation in progress.
PagerBot: Cloud event: nodepool maxNodes updated -> 120 (09:18:42Z)
Sam (sre): seeing new nodes provisioning; kubelet registrations starting. pending pods decreasing from 62 -> 18 in ~3m.
Ava (support): customers notified: "We increased capacity; your requests should recover shortly. We'll update if anything else." responses calmer.
Maya (oncall): good. Sam, can you evict the obvious noisy jobs? reduce head-of-queue hogs.
Sam (sre): yes — found 3 long-running batch jobs from internal test team with high GPU request. marking them preemptible and evicting: `kubectl delete pod <id>` for low-priority. Pods freed ~3 GPUs.
Devon (infra): autoscaler reports desired_nodes=96, current_nodes=92, scaling continues.
PagerBot: Metrics update: queue_length=124 -> 42 over 12 minutes, throttled=432 -> 38, 503 rate falling.
Maya (oncall): customer impact assessment: 6 customers reported incidents, 3 saw retries timeouts. Severity: P1 for infra team response; external comms handled by Ava.
Ava (support): filed CS tickets and created status page note draft. will post after you approve wording.
Maya (oncall): approve draft. mention ETA for full recovery ~30m, note manual cap bump performed, no data loss.
Sam (sre): follow-ups: 1) investigate autoscaler policy to avoid single-pool max causing outage; 2) add a fallback route to route some low-priority requests to smaller quantized model on different pool; 3) throttle-heavy tenants by token budget.
Devon (infra): action: create a safety-exception ticket to allow autoscaler to burst to 150 nodes during spikes for 48h while we patch the control plane.
Maya (oncall): handoff: I'll stay on until stabilized or until 10:00 UTC; if it still looks choppy hand off to night oncall @sam-night.
Sam (sre): noted. leaving monitoring charts and a quick alert rule change to trigger if pending pods > 40 for more than 5m.
OpsBot: Runbook reminder — record all commands executed in the incident log.
Maya (oncall): recording steps: manual cap bumped from 80->120 at 09:18Z; evicted 3 low-priority pods; autoscaler desired=96 -> stable; queue reduced. final verification in progress.
Ava (support): final customer update posted on status page. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0315-172
Sam (sre): post-incident TODOs assigned: tune autoscaler policies, add per-tenant backpressure, add an alert for nodepool maxNodes nearly reached.
Maya (oncall): closing loop: if anything regresses ping me immediately. good job team :thumbsup:
PagerBot: Incident INC-2026-0315-172 acknowledged closed by Maya (oncall) 09:45:23Z
